$comment: R-005 infrastructure ground truth for Brussels metro. Public facts only; unknown geometry stays unknown/design_model.

facts.limitations: Nominal system value; no public load/voltage-drop model is inferred.
Contact face, offset from track centreline, conductor profile, polarity and sectioning are not established by the checked source.
Infrastructure statistic, not track length and not a power-network topology map.
STIB footnote excludes the Delta and Demets complexes; no geometry, turnout ratio/radius or interlocking logic follows from this count.
STIB footnote excludes the Delta and Demets complexes; the statistic does not reveal block boundaries or signal aspects.
The source table does not split this 120 count into metro-only versus tram. Do not store it as 120 metro substations without another source.
STIB says a metro travels up to 72 km/h in tunnel. This is not proof of vehicle design Vmax or a limit on every track segment.
Do not make 40 km/h a universal station-entry rule without route/signal/speed-profile data.
General safety statement, not a precise measured dimension for every platform.
Confirms categories of required infrastructure, not their exact dimensions on existing lines 1/5.

track_gauge_mm.notes: 1435 mm is widely published and plausible, but R-005 did not confirm it in a primary STIB/Brussels Region/CAF source. Do not treat as spec yet.

third_rail_contact_geometry.notes: Exact contact face/top-bottom-side arrangement not established by checked primary source.

T-210: Reserve envelope for a third rail but keep exact rail position/profile design_model until sourced.
T-211: Use 900 V/third-rail as hazard metadata; do not present a guessed third-rail offset as STIB geometry.
T-310: 900 V may be system metadata; do not infer current limits, sectioning or voltage-drop behaviour without data.
T-313: Electric switches and signalling posts are source-backed facts; their exact layout and interlocking remain design_model/unknown.
speed_profiles: 72 km/h tunnel and 40 km/h station-entry statements are cross-checks, not universal hard-coded limits.
